resources.string: Small rituals that help you be who you meant to be.

string-array.name: thr_leave_cues
string-array.item: Breathe out longer than you breathe in.
Whatever happened before stays on the other side of this door.
You don\'t have to finish that conversation now.

resources.string: Nobody needs anything from you for a few seconds. Just be still.
A reminder at the moment one role ends and another begins: coming home, before a call, picking up the kids.
No thresholds scheduled. Pick the moments of the day when you switch roles.
Don\'t answer yet. Whatever you say in the next minute, anger says for you. Close your mouth, put the phone down, take a step back.
Four counts in, hold for seven, eight counts out. Three times.
You are a mountain. Weather passes over it; the mountain stays.

string-array.name: sos_ground_steps
string-array.item: Press both feet into the floor and feel its weight hold you.
Name three things you can see right now.
Unclench your jaw and let your hands open.
Let your shoulders drop away from your ears.

resources.string: Leaving a scene is not losing it. Pick a line to step out with.

string-array.name: sos_exit_lines
string-array.item: I need ten minutes. I\'ll come back and we\'ll finish this.
This matters to me, so I want to talk about it calmly. Give me a moment.
I\'m too angry to say anything useful right now. Let\'s pick this up in an hour.
I hear you. I need to think before I answer.
Let\'s stop here for now. I\'m not walking away from you, just from the shouting.

resources.string: Who do you come back as?
When the wave passes, pick the role you return to the scene in.
A hard conversation goes better when you have already walked through it once, in the role you want to be in.
Asking my boss for a raise
For us to agree on a date, without either of us getting defensive
The sharp remark that would end it badly
If it goes badly, I step out with
Let\'s take a break and come back to this tomorrow.
What happened, what worked, what you\'d do differently
The notes for this conversation will be gone.
Close your eyes. Where does it happen? See the room, the light, where you sit or stand.
Picture them in front of you. Their face, their mood today. Remember what you want from this.
Before you speak, become %1$s. Straighten up, slow your breath, soften your face.
Hear yourself say it calmly, at an easy pace.
They push back, or say something that stings. Feel it, and stay in the role. If you need to, step out with your line.
Picture the end: you said what mattered and stayed yourself. Notice how that feels.
Each role sees the question from its own corner. Hear them all, then let your core decide.
Do I take the job in another city?
Who sits on the council (pick %1$d to %2$d)
Which of your values matter most here, and what do they say?
What I decide, and the first step

string-array.name: letter_prompts
string-array.item: What do you see in me that I forget?
What did I do lately that you were proud of?
Where did I let you go quiet?
What do you ask of me this week?

resources.string: On my best day, they would say…
At my eightieth birthday, I want to hear…
How they would describe you, in their words
What you hope they say in their toast

string-array.name: shadow_talk_questions
string-array.item: What do you want when you take over?
What are you afraid would happen if you stepped back?
What do you need from me?

resources.string: My grandmother, a coach, a character from a book
How they speak, what they notice, what they never do
The one habit you will try this week
What you wrote will be gone.
Something small you can do anywhere without anyone noticing.
A word or a short line you say to yourself with the gesture.
A moment when you were %1$s at your best. Where were you, what did you do, how did it feel?
The evening I stayed calm when…
Make the gesture, say the word, and relive the memory while you hold the circle for ten seconds.
One per line. They repeat in order through the act.
This role already has an act in progress.
Tap a past day to mark it if you forgot.
The days you did stay counted.
Its days will no longer count toward the role.
